briefing.summary: CRAC-B-07 discharge temp alarm (38.1°C) — high confidence clogged air filter based on exact pattern match with INC-2024-0142 three months ago.
briefing.severity_assessment: P3 — Warning. Redundant cooling capacity in Zone B provides buffer. Rack inlet temps in Zone B remain nominal. Estimated 2h before rack inlet temps are affected if not resolved.

probable_causes.cause: Clogged air filter restricting airflow across evaporator coil
probable_causes.basis: Exact match with INC-2024-0142 (Sep 2024): same unit, same symptom profile (discharge temp + zone humidity rise), filter was overdue. Zone B is on monthly replacement schedule — last logged replacement was 6 weeks ago.
Occurred once on this unit (INC-2024-0318) but only after filter was confirmed clean. Subcooling anomaly not present in sensor data. Proceed to refrigerant check only if filter is clean.

correlated_signals.signal: Zone B humidity rising 45% → 58% over last 40 min
correlated_signals.relevance: Reduced airflow from clogged filter causes moisture to accumulate rather than circulate — consistent with filter obstruction pattern.
Mild thermal bleed from adjacent Zone B. Not yet actionable but confirms Zone B heat load is increasing.

similar_incidents.summary: Same unit, same symptom. Root cause: clogged FLT-2248. Resolved in 45 min.
Same unit, high discharge temp — turned out to be low refrigerant after filter ruled out. Second hypothesis.

recommended_actions.action: Verify discharge temp with handheld infrared thermometer at CRAC-B-07 front vent
recommended_actions.reason: Rule out sensor drift before dispatching. Takes 2 min.

recommended_actions.action: Inspect air filter through front access panel (T-25 torx, 4 screws)
recommended_actions.reason: Most probable cause based on history and schedule. Filter stock: Maintenance Room B, shelf 3, bin FLT-2248.

recommended_actions.action: Replace filter with FLT-2248. Check evaporator coil surface for dust — clean with compressed air if fouled.
recommended_actions.reason: Standard resolution per INC-2024-0142. Monitor discharge temp for 10 min after restart.

recommended_actions.action: If filter is clean, proceed to refrigerant pressure check via service port SP-B07-R
recommended_actions.reason: Second hypothesis per SOP-REFRIG-001. Nominal low-side: 118–125 PSI.

required_parts: FLT-2248 air filter (check van stock, or Maintenance Room B shelf 3)
briefing.escalation: None required unless rack inlet temps in Zone B exceed 32°C before team arrives, or discharge temp reaches 42°C+ indicating potential compressor stress.

briefing.summary: PDU-A-03 intermittent voltage sag (228V → 219V) — two hypotheses: capacitor degradation (70% probable, matches vendor bulletin VB-2024-03) or sensor drift (20% probable). Cross-check with multimeter first.
briefing.severity_assessment: P3 — Warning. Redundant PDU-A-04 is online and can absorb full load (currently at 18% capacity). No service interruption risk if transfer needed. Escalate to P2 if voltage drops below 215V.

probable_causes.cause: Degraded capacitor module (CAP-M12) in power conditioning stage
probable_causes.basis: Matches INC-2023-0298 pattern: same PDU model, same voltage sag profile (intermittent, gradual worsening). Vendor Bulletin VB-2024-03 specifically identifies PDU-A-03 (serial AP8853-2019-0447) as affected unit in the 2019 capacitor batch advisory.
INC-2024-0201 showed 9V sensor drift on PDU-A-02 after firmware update. Always eliminate this hypothesis first — multimeter cross-check takes 2 minutes and prevents unnecessary hardware callout.
PDU-A-04 (redundant, same feed) shows no fluctuation. Rules out upstream supply as the cause.

correlated_signals.signal: UPS-A-01 battery temp rising 22.1°C → 24.1°C over 2 hours
correlated_signals.relevance: UPS battery reacts to voltage instability by drawing more current — consistent with upstream PDU voltage sag. Not dangerous at current level but confirms PDU issue is real.
Redundant PDU on same feed shows no fluctuation — eliminates upstream supply fault, points to PDU-A-03 hardware.

similar_incidents.summary: PDU-A-01 (same model batch), same voltage sag pattern. Root cause: capacitor degradation. Resolved with CAP-M12 replacement in 120 min.
PDU-A-02 voltage alarm was sensor drift, not hardware fault. Resolved with recalibration in 30 min. Multimeter cross-check was the diagnostic step.

recommended_actions.action: Measure voltage at PDU-A-03 output bus with handheld multimeter (Fluke 117 or equivalent)
recommended_actions.reason: Eliminates sensor drift hypothesis in 2 minutes. If multimeter reads 225–229V while PDU monitor reads 219V, it's sensor drift — recalibrate, no parts needed.

recommended_actions.action: If multimeter confirms sag: visually inspect capacitor bank at rear panel bay C for bulging, discolouration, or electrolyte residue
recommended_actions.reason: VB-2024-03 advisory for this unit. Visual inspection confirms capacitor failure without any disassembly.

recommended_actions.action: Replace CAP-M12 capacitor module per MANUAL-PDU-A03 Section 5.2 (discharge capacitors first — 1kΩ resistor required)
recommended_actions.reason: Standard repair for this failure mode. Estimated 2h with failover to PDU-A-04.

recommended_actions.action: Before opening PDU: confirm PDU-A-04 can absorb full Zone A load. Transfer load if needed before working on PDU-A-03.
recommended_actions.reason: PDU-A-04 at 18% capacity — has ample headroom. Safe to transfer.

required_parts: CAP-M12 capacitor module (check warehouse stock — APC will supply free replacement per VB-2024-03, contact APC support)
briefing.estimated_resolution_time: 30 min (if sensor drift) or 2 hours (if capacitor replacement needed)
briefing.escalation: Notify facility manager immediately if voltage drops below 215V before team arrives. Activate UPS bypass if available.

briefing.summary: 4 alarms across Zones C+D in 6 minutes — individual CRAC and rack alarms are symptoms. Root cause is upstream: CHILLER-01 (Loop 2) supply temp rose from 7°C to 14°C over 20 min, indicating pump failure or chiller fault. This matches INC-2023-0089 exactly.
briefing.severity_assessment: P1 — Critical. All CRAC units in Zones C and D are affected. Chilled water supply at 14°C (nominal: 7°C). Rack inlet temps already at 35–36°C. 30-minute window before load shedding becomes necessary.

probable_causes.cause: CHILLER-01 Loop 2 circulation pump failure or significant flow reduction
probable_causes.basis: CHILLER-01 supply temp rose 7°C → 14°C over 20 min while all Zones C+D CRAC units degraded simultaneously. Zones A+B (Loop 1) are unaffected. Pattern is identical to INC-2023-0089 (pump bearing failure). Key diagnostic: if standby pump is activated and supply temp recovers, confirms pump as root cause.
Less likely than pump failure given the gradual temperature rise (compressor fault would typically be more abrupt) but cannot be ruled out without visual inspection at plant.

correlated_signals.signal: CHILLER-01 supply water temp: 7°C → 14°C over 20 min (threshold: 10°C)
correlated_signals.relevance: This is the root cause signal. Supply temp rising while pump should be running indicates pump failure or severe flow restriction.

correlated_signals.signal: CRAC-C-02 discharge temp: 25°C → 43°C over 2 hours (compressor fault at 09:06)
correlated_signals.relevance: CRAC is trying to compensate for warm supply water. Compressor fault is a consequence, not the cause.
Second CRAC on Loop 2 showing identical degradation — confirms systemic supply issue, not individual unit fault.
Zone D CRAC degrading simultaneously — spans both zones on Loop 2. Rules out zone-specific cause.
CRAC units struggling to control humidity when cooling supply is degraded. Secondary symptom of chiller failure.
Loop 1 (CHILLER-02) unaffected. Confirms fault is isolated to Loop 2 infrastructure.

similar_incidents.summary: CHILLER-01 pump bearing failure caused cascading thermal event across Zones C+D. 4-hour resolution. Key lesson: do not dispatch to individual CRAC units — go directly to chiller plant.

recommended_actions.action: IMMEDIATELY: Notify facility manager and on-call mechanical lead. Do not wait.
recommended_actions.reason: P1 protocol per SOP-CRIT-001. 30-minute window before load shedding decision.

recommended_actions.action: DO NOT restart CRAC-C-02 or other faulted CRAC units.
recommended_actions.reason: They will fault again immediately if chilled water supply is degraded. Restarting is wasted time and risks compressor damage.

recommended_actions.action: Primary team: Go directly to Chiller Plant. Check CHILLER-01 pump status (primary + standby). Verify chilled water flow rate (nominal: 850 LPM). If primary pump shows fault, activate standby pump via control panel (green STANDBY button).
recommended_actions.reason: This is the root cause. Standby pump switchover may restore cooling within 15 min, as in INC-2023-0089.

recommended_actions.action: Secondary team: Stage at Zone C/D entrance. Monitor rack inlet temps via BMS. Prepare for emergency load shedding per PROC-LOADSHED-CD.
recommended_actions.reason: Rack C-12 at 35.5°C, C-15 at 36.2°C. Shedding trigger: 38°C, or 30 min elapsed without chiller recovery.

recommended_actions.action: If standby pump does not restore supply temp within 10 min, escalate to mechanical lead for chiller compressor inspection.
recommended_actions.reason: Pump activation failure suggests deeper chiller plant fault requiring specialist intervention.

required_parts: None initially — standby pump is already installed. Parts TBD after root cause confirmed at plant.
briefing.estimated_resolution_time: 15–30 min if standby pump activation succeeds. 4+ hours if chiller compressor fault.
briefing.escalation: Facility manager and on-call mechanical lead: notify immediately. IT operations coordinator: notify now to prepare for possible load shedding. CTO on-call: notify if load shedding of production racks becomes necessary.
